statements.status_notes: nghttpx, the HTTP/2 proxy shipped with nghttp2, through 1.69.0 forwarded an HTTP/1.1 Upgrade request that also carries a Content-Length header and a body onto reusable keep-alive backend connections, so a backend that resolves the ambiguous message in the attacker's favour allows HTTP request smuggling and response-queue poisoning. Upstream fixed it in nghttp2 1.70.0 with https://github.com/nghttp2/nghttp2/commit/ab28105c4a0197da24f8bfc414bc116055249e1e (nghttpx: Tighten up CONNECT and HTTP Upgrade handling); see https://github.com/advisories/GHSA-xrr7-82jr-v58x. The DHI Alpine 3.23 nghttp2 package ships nghttpx as /usr/bin/nghttpx in every published build, built from the Alpine aports nghttp2 recipe. Inspected nghttpx in every published build on x86_64 and aarch64 (1.68.0-r0 to 1.71.0-r0): its version string matches the package version, and the request checks the fix adds, identified by their log messages ('Request body for Upgrade request is not allowed' and 'transfer-encoding and content-length are not allowed in CONNECT or upgrade request'), are present in 1.70.0-r0 and later builds and absent from every earlier build.
